stem: A 8-year-old girl is brought to the ED because of worsening left facial asymmetry. Two weeks ago she was diagnosed with left-sided facial droop and given prednisolone, but the droop has worsened and she now has mild slurred speech and increasing clumsiness. On examination she has: elevated BP, wide-based gait, inability to tandem walk, positive Romberg, vertical downbeat nystagmus, a complete left facial palsy involving both upper and lower face, rightward palate elevation, dysdiadochokinesia, and a coarse intention tremor. Her hearing and vision are normal. Based on her presentation, what is the MRI most likely to depict?

options.text: Bleed in the distribution of the left middle cerebral artery
Enhancement of the Facial nerve on the left but otherwise a normal brain

explanation: The combination of progressive cerebellar signs, elevated blood pressure, cranial nerve dysfunction, and worsening facial palsy suggests a posterior fossa tumour causing mass effect and brainstem/cerebellar involvement. This is more consistent with a posterior fossa mass than isolated facial nerve palsy or stroke.
rationale: Posterior fossa tumour with raised intracranial pressure and cerebellar/brainstem signs.

optionExplanations.A: An MCA bleed would typically cause acute contralateral weakness, aphasia, or cortical signs, not progressive cerebellar and posterior fossa findings.
optionExplanations.B: Isolated facial nerve enhancement would fit Bell palsy, but this child has multiple cerebellar and brainstem signs.
optionExplanations.C: Cerebellar hypoplasia is congenital and would not present with new progressive focal neurological deficits.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: progressive ataxia, downbeat nystagmus, cranial nerve palsy, and raised BP point to a posterior fossa mass.

source.questionTextHtml:
An 8 year old girl is brought into ED because of concern regarding facial asymmetry that is getting worse. The girl saw her GP 2 weeks ago with left sided facial droop and was given a course of steroids. When she returned to the GP this morning he was concerned that the droop was worse and he thought her speech had become a little slurred. He

wasn’t

sure if this was related so he sent her in for review. Her mother comments that this morning the girl was very clumsy and dropped her breakfast bowel full of cereal and then fell twice down the front steps on the way to the car. She has been a previously well child and competes at state for gymnastics. Her only medication has been prednisolone.

On examination her BP is 120/70 (elevated). She is afebrile and her HR is 100 bpm. Her height and weight are on the 50th centile. Her gait is wide based and although she can walk up on her heels and toes, she cannot perform tandem gait. When you get her to stand with her legs together and then close her eyes, she falls back immediately. Her vision is normal and she has normal discs. She has vertical nystagmus on looking down. She has a complete left facial palsy involving both the upper and lower portions of her face. Her hearing is grossly normal. When you look at her palate, you notice it pulls up towards the right. Her tongue moves normally, as do her neck muscles. She cannot perform rapidly alternating hand movements and on finger-nose finger testing you note she develops a coarse intention tremor. Her limb exam is otherwise normal.

Based on her presentation you think that an MRI is likely to depict:

Instructions

Question 4 - 6 relate to this quiz

Case 2

A 5-year old girl is brought in by her mother to see you because her teacher has been concerned that she has been having ‘day-dreams’ in choir practise and also during class. Her mother has also noted ‘day dreams’ which have been occurring mid-sentence associated with staring off in the distance. The ‘day dreams’ last a few seconds and then she is back to normal and continues on with her sentence. She doesn’t fall and doesn’t get sleepy after the events. She has no colour change. The girl is otherwise developmentally normal and got a good mid-year report from school. On examination her height and weight are on the 75

th

centile. She has a completely normal examination. You get the patient to blow up a balloon in your office and she has a staring spell that lasts 5seconds before she completely recovers.
